The four tangent Cauchy equalities plus total mass0 imply theta=eta_measure/D4 annihilates EVERY polynomial of degree<=4: P2/R+P2/Q spans P4/(RQ) because R,Q are coprime quadratics.

The inward y-normal is mean_E(t)-mean_O(t)>=0. Since theta kills P4, this is theta(t^5)>=0. The x-normal also gives theta(1/t)<=0, though the sign-count reduction below already uses the first inequality alone.

Ordered active hulls are E1,O1,E2,O2,E3,O3. On E1 the sign of theta is positive and on O3 negative. In each middle hull O1,E2,O2,E3 its sign is NEGATIVE left of the selected root and POSITIVE right. A strictly improper root LEFT of its actual band gives only positive active theta; a root RIGHT gives only negative active theta. Both-side activity is possible only for a root STRICTLY INSIDE its own actual band.

If all active even middle hulls were proper, the first outward even hull plus the two actual even bands would place H_E in CE_infinity; H_O=H_E+eta_normal*ell_infinity is then in the same cone. Thus H_O failure requires an ACTIVE improper even root. Similarly K_O failure requires an ACTIVE improper odd root, since the q3=infinity tail is safe for CO_zero. There are therefore at least TWO active improper middle hulls, one of each parity, and at most TWO middle hulls with both signs.

Elementary sign-variation lemma: theta nonzero and annihilating P4 must have at least5 sign changes. If it has exactly5, choose a monic degree5 polynomial with one root in each change gap. Its integral has the STRICT sign of theta on the last sign block, but equals theta(t^5)>=0. Hence exactly5 changes require LAST sign positive (and first negative). No finite enumeration/interpreter is used.

Let r count active hulls and B count middle hulls active on both sides. Variation is at most r+B-1. If B<=1: with no outer hull active it is<=4; with exactly one outer it is<=5 but a5-change pattern has the wrong first/last sign; with both outers it is odd<=5 and ends negative. Every case contradicts the lemma. Hence B=2, all FOUR middle hulls are active, exactly two middle roots are strictly improper and the other two lie strictly inside their actual bands with both-side contacts.

With k=0,1,2 active outer hulls, maximal variation is5+k. Smaller allowed variation is excluded by the same last-sign test and outer signs, so EVERY possible inter-hull and within-proper-hull sign change must occur. The first middle sign is negative. A proper block is(-,+) and resets the required next start to negative. The first one-sign improper block must therefore be negative; it makes the next required start positive, so the NEXT middle block must be the second improper one, positive. Thus the two improper middle roots are ADJACENT, the earlier RIGHT of its actual band and the later LEFT of its actual band.

The only residual patterns are (q1,p2) both in(d1,a2), with d1<q1<p2<a2; OR (p2,q2) both in(b2,c2), with b2<p2<q2<c2; OR (q2,p3) both in(d2,a3), with d2<q2<p3<a3. The OTHER two middle roots lie strictly inside their actual own bands and have contacts on both sides. This is a necessary actual-stationary failure localization, not proof that any pattern is realizable.
